title: EuroTrip
synopsis: Graduation week. A penpal in Berlin. Three friends, one rail pass, and an unwise budget. The plane lands in London at 6 a.m. Go.

nodes.text: You land in London with two backpacks too many and one good plan. The plan involves Mieke.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Sights.
There is no taking “Skip to Paris” back. Train shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: The hostel manager is a man named Vinnie. Vinnie has a very specific energy.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Friend.
“Sleep with one eye open” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Wise.

nodes.text: Your friend Scott offends a Manchester United fan in a pub. The pub becomes a chase. The chase becomes a story.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Smart.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Brave—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The ferry is bouncy. Cooper is seasick. You realize travel friendship requires more grace than you expected.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Friend—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Read on deck.” The story records the instinct as “Self” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Paris is, against all the cliches, exactly what they said. You are, somehow, both nineteen and exactly the right age.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Touristy—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Vibey—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: You and your friend Jenny adopt a street mime. The mime has, somehow, a phone number.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Whimsy.
There is no taking “Tip the mime, move on” back. Practical shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Bicycles. Canals. A man named Hennie selling, technically, tours.

choices.consequence: “Take the tour” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Trust.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Independent.

nodes.text: Rome on a Saturday is, in fact, a kind of carnival. The Trevi Fountain has a coin policy.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Throw the coin.” The story records the instinct as “Tradition” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Cheap.

nodes.text: A pickpocket lifts Scott's wallet. Scott, in a moment of clarity, lifts it back.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Celebrate.” The story records the instinct as “Win” and carries it forward.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Even.

nodes.text: Scott is mistaken for a tourist who is, separately, evading a debt. The Vatican guard is gentle but firm.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Explain.” The story records the instinct as “Process” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Run.” The story records the instinct as “Comedy” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Berlin is colder than expected. Mieke's address is, technically, valid.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Brave.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Wise.

nodes.text: Mieke opens the door. She is taller than you imagined and exactly as wonderful.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
“Try to charm her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Funny.

nodes.text: You and Scott and Cooper and Jenny end up at a club whose doorman judges you with great efficiency. Jenny, somehow, gets in.

choices.consequence: “Wait outside for Jenny” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Friend.
“Find another club” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Adventure.

nodes.text: Overnight train to Bratislava. Cheap. The bunk is, technically, a shelf. Cooper sleeps anyway.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Smart.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Story.

nodes.text: Bratislava is, of course, much cheaper than your guidebook promised. You and the boys eat very well.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wise—follows you into whatever comes next.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Schedule.

nodes.text: A bar with a robot bartender. The robot bartender is, you realize, just a man in a costume. The man is friendly.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Vibe.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Style—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Italian train strike. You and the gang sleep in a station with a stray dog. The dog likes Cooper best.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Hilarious.
“Find a hotel” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Adult.

nodes.text: By accident you end up at a small Pope audience. The Pope, somehow, blesses Cooper specifically.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Story.
There is no taking “Just be there” back. Holy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Mieke catches up with you in Venice. She is, against all odds, also into Scott. He realizes, late, that he likes her too.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Friend—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Joke about it forever.” The story records the instinct as “Tone” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Last night before flights home. You sit at a hostel bar in Lisbon. You realize the summer is, finally, ending.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Toast everyone.” The story records the instinct as “Sentiment” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Quiet.

nodes.text: You land in London again on the way back. You are, technically, the same person. You are, technically, not.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Go home” back. Practical shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Brave.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You go home. You start senior year a slightly different person. The trip becomes the reference point. Your friends, ten years from now, will quote it at parties.
You stay an extra week. The week, somehow, becomes a month. You almost don't come home. You realize, in the end, you can come back. You will.
Scott marries Mieke. You are the best man. The wedding is in Berlin. The toast is the longest of your life. You realize the trip was, somehow, a love story you didn't know you were in.
